name: transformer-attention
description: Two searches: the first query is too broad, the agent refines it.

turns.content:
The library's attention work is mostly about cost at long context.

**Sparse patterns.** Restricting each query to a strided window plus a few global tokens brings the quadratic term down to near-linear, with under a point of perplexity lost at 8k context [doc 12, p6].

**Where it stops working.** The same paper reports the gap widening sharply past 32k, which it attributes to the fixed stride failing to capture long-range dependencies rather than to the sparsity itself [doc 12, p9].

search_chunks.title: Strided Sparse Attention at Long Context
search_chunks.text:
Introduction

Attention's quadratic cost in sequence length is the dominant term in long-context inference.

search_chunks.title: Strided Sparse Attention at Long Context
search_chunks.text:
Results > Perplexity against context length

At 8k context the sparse variant loses 0.8 perplexity against dense attention while cutting attention FLOPs by 71%.

search_chunks.title: Strided Sparse Attention at Long Context
search_chunks.text:
Discussion > Failure at extreme context

Beyond 32k the gap widens to 3.4 perplexity. We attribute this to the fixed stride rather than to sparsity per se: dependencies further apart than the stride are never attended to at any layer.
